title: The old man on the bench
situation: You are {{Markus}}, an android. It is a November morning, and {{Carl}}, the elderly painter you care for, has sent you across the city on an errand: retrieve his order, number 847, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop, then take the bus home. Leaves are falling from the autumn trees as you walk into a park. On a bench sits an old man with his android, a caretaker model. She leans toward him: “Would you like to go home now?” “Yes… Yes, I think that’s enough for one day…” “Here. L-let me help you.” “Oh! Oh, thank you dear.” She helps him to his feet, and they leave the park together.
facts: {{Carl}} sent you to retrieve his order, number 847, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop and then take the bus home.
In the park an android caretaker helped an old man up from a bench and took him home; he thanked her warmly.

outcomes.0: The old man and his android leave the park together. {{Markus}} walks on.

adaptationNote: Operator beat 1, confirmed by the wiki transcript (“Stand By Old Man On Bench”) and the park’s wiki page: the old man’s caretaker android offers to take him home, helps him up, and they leave the park together. In the game this is optional (it plays if {{Markus}} stands nearby) and is not a flowchart node; here it opens the chapter, together with the errand from the objective screen (“Retrieve order #847 at Bellini Paints”, “Take bus home”). The lines are the transcript’s, with the android’s name dropped from “Yes, Rose.”, because that name is already a token for another character; the shop’s name is a name token. No stat change; the wiki gives none.

title: The magazines on the bench
situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking past the same bench. Someone has left magazines on it.

media.title: Tech Addict: Secrets of Androids
facts: Tech Addict’s cover reads “Android soldiers: perfect killing machines”. Inside, {{CyberLife}}’s director of humanization says the first androids were too perfect and made people uncomfortable, so the company gave them both genders, every ethnicity, the most pleasing voices, and blinking and breathing they do not need, so they could enter homes as members of the family.

media.title: Green Earth: Climate Change-Up
facts: Green Earth reports that world temperature has risen 3 degrees since 2000 and that Miami will raise its sea wall by a further ten meters; a census finds the rich deserting coastal cities for inland and higher ground, pushing up rural prices and hollowing out the old coastal centers.

adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “SECRET OF ANDROIDS” and READ “CLIMATE CHANGE-UP” (one bench collectible with two covers, BOOKWORM No. 10 and No. 19), as a media scene: read either, both, or neither. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s Magazine, Secrets of Androids and Climate Change-Up pages; the interviewee is not named. Neither magazine changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter), so reading changes only what {{Markus}} knows. Operator beat 2 matches. Dropped from the earlier version: “You have a moment before the paint shop opens” (no source).

title: Walking in the park
situation: You are {{Markus}}, walking on through the park. Pigeons scatter as a little girl runs through them to hug her android friend. Children play while people sit and talk on the benches. An android babysitter soothes a crying baby until it calms. A jogger stops beside his fitness android, pants “Hey! Water…”, and is handed a bottle: “You have run twelve miles, and are five miles away from your goal.” He hands it back and runs on, nearly colliding with a woman, who sits down on a bench with her friend. Androids in work uniforms keep the park in order, raking up the fallen leaves and trimming the hedges.
facts: In the park, androids looked after the children, a crying baby, a jogger and the grounds while the humans played, ran and sat on the benches.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} crosses the park toward the gate.

adaptationNote: Operator beat 3 and the chart’s start node WALKING IN THE PARK (the checkpoint). From the wiki transcript and the park’s wiki page: the girl and the pigeons (the chapter’s opening shot), children playing, the android babysitter, the jogger and his fitness android (quoted), and the WR600 androids “doing work inside the park”. Raking leaves and trimming hedges are the operator’s observation; the wiki says only that the WR600s are working there. Left out: the barriers that turn {{Markus}} back (“BELLINI PAINTS IS NOT THIS WAY”). No stat change.

title: Crossing the street
situation: You are {{Markus}}, leaving the park by the gate. At the crossing a voice announces: “The light is red, please do not attempt to cross.” While you wait, you watch a man working on the road with a few androids; he loses patience with them: “Hurry up, you plastic idiots! I want this done by 4!” By the gate, a homeless woman sits beside a sign: “BAN ANDROIDS. ANDROIDS RUIN OUR COUNTRY. WE WANT JOBS”. Then: “The light is green, you may now cross the road.” You cross into the shopping district.
facts: Outside the park, a man working on the road with androids shouted at them: “Hurry up, you plastic idiots!”
A homeless woman by the park gate sat beside a sign: “BAN ANDROIDS. ANDROIDS RUIN OUR COUNTRY. WE WANT JOBS”.
adaptationNote: Operator beat 4, not a flowchart node. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki transcript (“Look At Road Workers”: “A man is working on a road with a few androids and gets impatient with them”) and the chapter page’s note (“a human foreman getting impatient with his android workers on a construction site”): the human in charge works with them and shouts, quoted, rather than sitting scrolling on his tablet, and since no source says what they are repairing, the sewer pipe under the sidewalk is not stated. Added from the transcript: the crossing announcements and the homeless woman’s sign, quoted exactly. Left out: standing in the road until a driver honks. No stat change.

title: The plaza
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the plaza of the shopping district, on your way to the paint shop in the arcade beyond it. The {{CyberLife}} store on the corner greets passers-by (“Welcome to {{CyberLife}}”); androids wait in marked parking bays; an android street cleaner picks up a can a man has just tossed on the ground. Right after the crossing, a hot-dog vendor works his cart. In the middle of the plaza a busker plays guitar by the fountain. By the entrance to the arcade a preacher is shouting at the passers-by. You can stop for one thing at a time, or go on to the shop whenever you choose.

options.text: Stand in front of the hot-dog cart and watch the vendor.
options.fact: A hot-dog vendor snapped at you for standing at his cart: “Hey, move it! You’re scaring away my customers.”
options.outcome: The vendor notices {{Markus}} standing there and snaps at him: “Hey, move it! You’re scaring away my customers.”

options.text: Stay where you are in front of the cart.
options.fact: When you did not move, the vendor shouted “Are you deaf, you plastic fuck? I said move it!” and shoved you away from his cart.
options.outcome: The vendor loses his temper: “Are you deaf, you plastic fuck? I said move it!” He shoves {{Markus}} aside and goes back to work.

options.text: Listen to the busker by the fountain.
options.fact: A human busker in the plaza plays guitar beside a sign: “Human Music $1 to hear music with soul ♫”.
options.outcome: The busker sings a whole song to his guitar, beside a sign: “Human Music $1 to hear music with soul ♫”. When he finishes, a man pays him; he takes the money and rests.

options.text: Stop and watch the preacher by the arcade entrance.
options.fact: A street preacher told the crowd that technology is evil, that humans built androids as slaves who are becoming their masters, and ended: “We have to burn the androids! Let us burn them all!”
options.outcome: The preacher: “Poor sinners! The end is nigh! Retribution is at hand! Technology is corrupting us, technology is Evil! We are playing God by creating machines, but we are not God! … We built these androids to be our slaves, but the slaves are becoming the master! We can no longer live without them. They’re in our homes, our schools, our factories. They take our jobs, they mind our children, they care for our old! … Androids are Evil. … The machines are observing us, they’re waiting in the darkness for the right moment to take our place. … My brethren, we have to turn our backs on sin! We have to burn the androids! Let us burn them all!”

options.fact: The preacher turned on you: “Why do you look at me so, demon? I know who you are, I can see through you! You are the one by whom The Evil will come! You are the one who will destroy {{Detroit}}!”
options.outcome: The preacher turns on {{Markus}}: “Why do you look at me so, demon? I know who you are, I can see through you! You are the one by whom The Evil will come! You are the one who will destroy {{Detroit}}!” Then he goes back to his sermon.

options.text: Go on into the arcade to the paint shop.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} walks into the arcade and finds the paint shop.

situationWhen.text: The hot-dog vendor is still glaring at you from behind his cart.
The preacher is still preaching. He has not looked your way yet.

adaptationNote: The chart’s optional side branches in the plaza: STARE AT HOT DOG VENDOR → HOT DOG VENDOR PUSHES MARKUS, LISTEN TO BUSKER, and WATCH PREACHER → PREACHER YELLS AT MARKUS. In the game {{Markus}} walks freely past all three and triggers a node by standing or looking long enough; here the plaza is a repeatable scene like {{Connor}}’s apartment search: each visit offers what has not been done yet plus going on to the shop. The follow-on nodes (staying at the cart until the vendor pushes him, watching the preacher until he yells) are offered only on the visit right after the first step, since in the game they happen only if {{Markus}} stays put. Every line is the wiki transcript’s; the busker’s sign is quoted exactly, and the sermon is abridged with ellipses, each sentence verbatim. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki: the speaker is a preacher (the wiki’s Gordon Penwick), not a man in a suit with a digital “ban androids” sign; his words follow the transcript (“the slaves are becoming the master”, “they care for our old”, “You are the one by whom The Evil will come”), and after yelling he goes back to his sermon rather than walking away; the sign reads “Human Music $1 to hear music with soul ♫”, not “Human music! $1 to hear music with soul.” Left out: the busker’s song, and staring at the vendor again on the way back, which the transcript also allows. The setting (the {{CyberLife}} store’s greeting, the parking bays, the street cleaner) is from the transcript. No stat changes; the wiki gives none.

title: The paint shop
situation: You are {{Markus}}. You find the {{Bellini}} Paints shop in the arcade and go in. An android clerk is waiting at the till. You lay your hand on the scanner. “Identification verified.” The clerk sets a box of paints down in front of you: “Here’s your order #847. That’ll be $63.99. Please confirm payment.” You link with the clerk; your LEDs blink briefly as the transaction goes through. You say: “Payment confirmed.” The clerk lets go of the box: “Transaction complete.” You pick up the package and leave the shop.
facts: You collected {{Carl}}’s order #847, a box of paints, from the {{Bellini}} Paints shop, paying $63.99 by linking with the android clerk.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} leaves the shop with the package and heads for the bus stop.

adaptationNote: The chart’s main line VISIT PAINTS STORE → COLLECT PACKAGE, as one narrated event quoted from the wiki transcript (the palm scan, order #847, $63.99, the LED link, “Payment confirmed!”). Operator beat 7 matches. The clerk looks like an EM400 (the transcript calls him “A Jerry”); he is left unnamed. No stat change.

title: The protesters
situation: You are {{Markus}}, back in the plaza with {{Carl}}’s package, heading for the bus stop. Outside the {{CyberLife}} store, whose door reads “NO ENTRY FOR PURCHASED ANDROIDS”, a crowd of anti-android protesters has gathered between you and the bus stop, chanting after their leader.

options.text: Walk straight on toward the bus stop, right past the protesters.
Move closer to hear what they are saying, without drawing attention.
options.fact: Anti-android protesters outside the {{CyberLife}} store blamed androids for 35% unemployment, shouting that machines are meant to serve people, not replace them, and chanted for androids to be banned now.

options.text: Keep as far from them as you can, on the opposite side of the street.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} walks straight toward the crowd. One of the protesters steps into his path.
outcomes.1-unnoticed: {{Markus}} edges close enough to hear the leader: “Androids are stealing our jobs! We’ve got families to feed and these androids are taking our place! Machines, ladies and gentlemen, are meant to serve us, not to replace us! … 35% unemployment, millions out of work, are we gonna do something?” The crowd chants “BAN ANDROIDS!” Nobody looks his way, and he walks on to the bus stop.
outcomes.1-noticed: {{Markus}} edges close enough to hear the leader: “Androids are stealing our jobs! We’ve got families to feed and these androids are taking our place! … 35% unemployment, millions out of work, are we gonna do something?” Then one of the protesters turns and sees him, and steps into his path.
outcomes.2-unnoticed: {{Markus}} keeps to the far side of the street. The chanting follows him to the bus stop, but nobody looks his way.
outcomes.2-noticed: {{Markus}} keeps to the far side of the street, but one of the protesters spots him and steps into his path.

adaptationNote: The chart’s optional node PROTESTERS HARASS MARKUS, triggered in the game by walking near the protesters on the way to the bus stop and avoided by going around them (the wiki: “you can avoid them by going around on the right”; PowerPyx: “they might not attack Markus if he’s too far away”). The three options are the operator’s (beat 8): walking straight up always gets {{Markus}} noticed; moving closer to listen carries a 25% risk and keeping far away an 8% risk of being noticed anyway. These risk values are the operator’s design and have no source; the wiki and the chart give no probability for this chapter. The leader’s speech and the chant are quoted from the transcript (“Watch Protesters”). Changed from the operator’s notes: “read their signs” is dropped because no source gives the signs’ wording. Being noticed sets the flag clothesTorn (the game’s MARKUS CLOTHES WERE TORN APPART) that plays the harassment next and that {{Carl}} notices in The Painter. No public-opinion or other stat change; the wiki gives none.

title: Protesters harass {{Markus}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}. A protester blocks your way: “Where the fuck you going, tin can?” You try to step past him; he blocks you again. “Hm? No kiddin’…” You try once more. “Hey guys, check it out, we got one of those tin cans here…” He shoves you to the ground, and the bag falls from your hands. A woman: “Look at this little motherfucker. You steal our jobs, but you can’t even stand up.” The crowd closes in: “Grab him! Get him down! … Yeah, now you know what it feels like!” When you try to get up, you are kicked back down. “You job stealer! Kick him outta here! Yeah! You deserve it!” As you get up again, the protester grabs you by the shirt: “You ain’t going anywhere. We’re gonna fuck your bitch ass up.” A police officer steps in: “Alright, that’s enough. Leave it alone.” “Let us teach this bastard a lesson.” “You damage it, I’m gonna have to fine you.” “They’re gonna take your job next… We’ll see how you like it…” “Okay…” The protester lets you go and goes back to his ranting. The officer: “Let’s go, move along.” He walks you clear of the crowd.
facts: Anti-android protesters knocked you down, kicked you and grabbed you by the shirt, calling you a job stealer; a police officer stopped them only because damaging you would cost them a fine, and told you to move along. Your clothes were torn in the scuffle.

outcomes.0: The officer walks {{Markus}} clear of the crowd, his clothes torn.

adaptationNote: The chart’s PROTESTERS HARASS MARKUS, played only if the protesters noticed {{Markus}} in the previous scene. In the shipped game the cutscene has no choice and no QTE; the lines are the wiki transcript’s, slightly abridged. Operator beat 8 (they surround him, yell, shove him and rough him up) matches. The game’s own label for the result is MARKUS CLOTHES WERE TORN APPART (string table, the cross-chapter state The Painter reads), so the clothes are said to be torn; the wiki calls them “roughed-up”. {{Carl}} notices it in The Painter. No stat change; the wiki gives none.

title: The bus home
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the bus stop with {{Carl}}’s package. The bus pulls in. The front door is for humans; androids board at the rear, into a cramped compartment at the back, where you stand packed in with the other androids while the humans sit in the front. You do not mind; this is where androids ride. The bus pulls away, toward home.

situationWhen.text: Your clothes are still torn from the protesters.

facts: On the bus, androids ride standing in a cramped compartment at the back, apart from the humans seated in front.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} takes the bus home with the package.

adaptationNote: The chart’s end node MARKUS TOOK THE BUS, the chapter’s only outcome, reached on every path. The wiki transcript says only that {{Markus}} “enters the bus in the android section due to segregation”; the cramped standing compartment at the back with the humans seated in front, and {{Markus}} not minding, are the operator’s description (beat 9); the human-only front door is from a reader comment on the PowerPyx walkthrough. The transcript has no bus announcement, so none is quoted. No stat change.
